articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops a biblical 167 security fixes including a SharePoint zero-day and a Windows Defender flaw dubbed 'BlueHammer' — because apparently April showers bring CVE flowers. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day this year because Google's having a stellar security season.

articles.title: Meta U-turns on encryption push for Instagram as DMs go plaintext
articles.summary: 'Dirty Frag' Linux flaw breaks the cardinal rule of responsible disclosure — public root exploit with no patches and no CVE because someone couldn't keep their embargo pants on. Admins everywhere are having a very bad day.

articles.title: cPanel, WHM Release Fixes for Three New Vulnerabilities — Patch Now
articles.summary: Ollama's out-of-bounds read vulnerability (CVE-2026-[redacted]) lets unauthenticated attackers slurp entire process memory from 300,000+ servers. It's like leaving your diary open, but your diary contains everyone's secrets.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: ShinyHunters turned finals week into actual hell by breaching Canvas and holding student data hostage with a ransom demand plastered on login pages. Nothing says 'happy graduation' like your entire academic record being auctioned to the highest bidder.

articles.title: Congress Narrowed the GUARD Act, But Serious Problems Remain
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence pulled a sneaky router hack to mass-harvest Microsoft Office tokens — because why break into one account when you can steal authentication cookies by the thousands? Classic GRU efficiency.

articles.title: Canvas Got Hacked During Finals Week and Students Are Freaking Out
articles.summary: NVIDIA confirms GeForce NOW got pwned, exposing Armenian user data in what's probably the most geographically specific breach disclosure we've seen this month. Someone's targeting very specific gamers.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: The DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as an arrestable offense — but only if you're not the government, naturally. Peak hypocrisy from an administration that perfected the art of transparency avoidance.

articles.title: Hackers ate my homework: Educational SaaS Canvas down after cyberattack
articles.summary: Meta pulls a spectacular U-turn on Instagram encryption, going back to plaintext DMs after years of privacy promises. Zuckerberg apparently decided user privacy was just a phase he was going through.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after SMS phishing campaigns that would make the old-school social engineers weep with pride. Another legend bites the dust in federal court.

articles.title: U.S. Fuel Exports Hit Record High as Hormuz Crisis Reshapes Global Energy Flows
articles.summary: Anthropic's Mythos AI found thousands of zero-days across major OS and browsers, prompting the Fed chair to speed-dial bank CEOs in panic. When AI starts finding vulns faster than humans can patch them, we're officially in the cybersecurity singularity.
